sections.h2: Cash sale or listing in Colonie
sections.html:
It depends on what the house needs and how quickly you must move. Colonie is the most populous suburb of Albany, and plenty of owners there list the traditional way. Deferred repairs, tenants, a probate delay or a tax problem point toward a cash buyer who takes the house as is.

Listing the house means getting it ready, fitting in showings and then waiting for the buyer's bank. A cash sale replaces that with a walkthrough and a closing date you help choose. The price is usually lower than a top-dollar listing, so total up what each route leaves after the mortgage payoff, back taxes and closing costs before you decide.

  • List with an agent for a house that shows well and a schedule with room in it.
  • Sell without an agent if you have a buyer in hand and can manage the contract.
  • A cash offer fits an inherited house, a rental with difficult tenants, storm or fire damage, or a move on a fixed date.

Colonie sits north of Albany, with the Mohawk River along its northern line and the Hudson on the east. Interstates 87, 787 and 90 and US Route 9 cross it, and Albany International Airport lies inside the town. The town contains two incorporated villages, Colonie and Menands, plus hamlets such as Latham, Loudonville, Newtonville, Boght Corners, Verdoy and West Albany. Postwar suburban building took off here, and the population rose from 29,522 in 1950 to 69,147 in 1970. The 2020 count was 85,590 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is 86,837.

Residents 65 and older make up 20.4% of the population, so estate sales and downsizing are common reasons houses come to market here.

Six public school districts serve the town: South Colonie, North Colonie, Watervliet, Menands, Niskayuna and Mohonasen. South Colonie covers much of the west, including West Albany and the village of Colonie, while North Colonie, which feeds Shaker High School, serves Latham and most of Loudonville and Newtonville.

When you list or sell, name the district and the nearest park, because Colonie buyers shop by both. The Town runs the Mohawk River Park and Pool Complex and a Parks and Recreation program, which is worth passing along to a family relocating from outside the Capital Region.

The Receiver of Taxes mails the general tax bill on December 31, and it is payable in January without penalty. Colonie is a town of the first class, and its collector is an elected Receiver of Taxes and Assessments.

  • General bill: due January 1 to 31, then 1% in February and 2% in March.
  • April 1: unpaid general bills go to the Albany County Department of Finance.
  • School bills: mailed August 31, due in September, then 4% in October.
  • November 1: unpaid school bills go to the county, and after December 1 they move onto the next general bill with a 7% penalty.

The office collects school tax for five districts and also bills water for Latham Water, about 22,000 accounts twice a year, with a 5% penalty after 30 days. If a prior owner received an exemption they no longer qualified for, an exemption payback charge can show up on the bill. Ask the office for a duplicate bill and any open balance before closing.

Owners who are 65 or older, or disabled, and live in a one, two or three family house can name a third party to receive duplicate bills on form RP-923, which helps when an aging parent is selling. Counter hours stretch to 6 p.m. during the last five business days of January and September. If January 31 is a weekend day, payment is due the next Monday.

The Assessor's office in Memorial Town Hall, 534 New Loudon Road in Latham, runs the standard New York calendar. Exemptions and the taxable status date fall on March 1, the tentative roll is filed May 1, Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday in May and the final roll is filed July 1.

A complaint must reach the office by 8:00 p.m. on Grievance Day. A postmark that day does not count, and electronic service is refused. Colonie asks owners to come with a recent purchase contract, sales of similar homes nearby or a current appraisal, and the owner carries the burden of proof. Colonie's 2027 Grievance Day is in late May.

A sale that closes in the fall or winter still carries the status the house had on March 1, so check your exemptions before you list. Anything you hold now, such as a senior or disability exemption, does not transfer automatically to the buyer.

Owners who bought after March 2, 2015, or never claimed STAR on a primary home, are told to register for the STAR credit, which pays by check. The Basic STAR income limit is $250,000, and above that you need the credit. A buyer in that group should register after closing, and exemption forms are handed out at the Assessor's counter on weekdays during business hours.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Albany County
sections.html:
Albany County records deeds and mortgages, and deed and mortgage records since 1980 are searchable online. The seller usually pays state transfer tax at $2 for every $500 of price, and Form TP-584 must reach the county clerk within 15 days of delivering the deed. Confirm current recording fees with the clerk.

Setting up a Colonie sale in order: first confirm the amount owed on any mortgage, then pull your general and school tax bills, then decide whether the house is better sold as it stands or after repairs. For a house with tenants, read the lease for the term and the deposit before you talk to a buyer. For an estate, the person with authority to sign needs to be named early, since the title company will ask for the papers. Each of these steps is faster when you start with the paperwork in hand.

Latham Water bills twice a year, so check whether a water balance is open on the parcel. A balance left behind can follow the property, and the buyer's attorney will want it cleared. The Town's official website is townofcolonie.gov, so use that address when you look up departments.

Before you accept a cash offer, gather the deed, the latest general and school bills, a payoff statement for any loan, and the lease if there are tenants. The closing attorney uses them to order the title search and to split taxes between you and the buyer.

faqs.q: Will a cash buyer take a Colonie house with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Many will, but terms differ, so say so up front. Tell the buyer the lease dates, rent and deposit, and check your lease before you sign anything.

faqs.q: When is a Colonie property tax payment late?
faqs.a: After January 31. February adds 1% and March adds 2%, and on April 1 unpaid general bills go to the Albany County Department of Finance.

faqs.q: Does Colonie handle school taxes at Town Hall?
faqs.a: Yes for five districts. The Receiver of Taxes collects South Colonie, North Colonie, Menands, Niskayuna and Mohonasen bills, which are mailed August 31 and due in September.

faqs.q: What is the next Grievance Day in Colonie?
faqs.a: May 25, 2027. Complaints must be in the Assessor's office by 8:00 p.m. that day, and exemption forms are due March 1.

faqs.q: Which county office records a Colonie deed?
faqs.a: The Albany County Clerk. Form TP-584 goes with the deed, and the clerk can quote current fees.
